evidence: rule_sets.py:330 defines _COLUMN_LOCAL = (CompareRule, IsNullRule, IsNotNullRule, AnyOfRule, AllOfRule). Each declares `kind: Literal["..."]` (lines 200, 235, 242, 259, 266), a bare Literal with no Annotated wrapper. Line 434 reads kind.model_fields["kind"].annotation.__args__[0]. In pydantic v2 (pyproject.toml:36 pins >=2.6,<3), FieldInfo.annotation holds the evaluated annotation with Annotated metadata stripped. That holds even under `from __future__ import annotations` (line 17), because pydantic resolves the string annotation. So it is Literal['compare'] etc., and __args__[0] is the plain string. The join at 433-436 therefore lists the allowed kinds. Caveat: no uv.lock or other lock file was found in the head view, so I checked against the declared range, not a locked version. rule_sets.py:636-643 builds exp.Not(this=exp.Paren(this=exp.Is(col, Null))). The sqlglot generator emits NOT then the Paren as '(...)', giving NOT (x IS NULL); the repo's unit test (tests/unit/test_row_rule_additions.py:225) asserts that text. The sqlglot parser (.venv sqlglot/parser.py:1226) parses NOT as Not(this=_parse_equality()), and a parenthesized operand yields exp.Paren, so the re-parse gives Not(Paren(Is)). The test at test_row_rule_additions.py:239-245 asserts that shape under mysql. prove_compiled_rule (safety/rule_sets.py:445-450) compares _shape(reparsed) with _shape(body) and raises only on mismatch, so the tree is accepted. I could not execute code (no shell), so this rests on reading the parser and the test, not a run.

rule_sets.py:636-643 builds Not(Paren(Is(col, NULL))), matching the comment. Per MySQL 8.0 operator precedence docs, HIGH_NOT_PRECEDENCE raises NOT above comparison operators (IS, BETWEEN, etc.), so a bare `NOT x IS NULL` parses as `(NOT x) IS NULL`; the parentheses prevent that. Verified from the code and my recollection of the MySQL docs, not by running MySQL. Absolute-claim trace: input `NOT deleted_at IS NULL` with non-NULL deleted_at would parse as `(NOT deleted_at) IS NULL`; the Paren node avoids that.
